gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, in DashCamTalk reviewer Vortex Radar's test of the Botslab G980H four-camera kit (posted 2026-04-23, edited 2026-10-16), parking motion detection 'only works on front cam, side cams won't trigger', and that the front camera drops to 1620p25 while the side cameras are fitted. The '4K' figure (2160p25) only applies in 2–3 channel mode.
standout_why: I compared against the cited DashCamTalk 'Best Dash Cams of 2026' (read 2026-11-21). Its only 4-channel entry is the Vantrue N5S, listed as Front, Rear, Interior, Interior Rear. It has no Botslab, Rexing or REDTIGER entry and no measured figures. I also checked the cited Thinkware multiplexer support article (no camera resolutions, no parking-trigger detail) and caraudioradar.com's 'Best Dash Cams With Left and Right Cameras' (2026-10-23). That page covers a 'BOTSLAB 4-Channel 360°' but gives no per-channel frame rate, no bitrate, and nothing on which cameras trigger parking motion detection. ChatGPT's second answer named the G980H 'best overall' for '3K front recording and adjustable side views', but none of its sources says side cameras don't trigger a parked recording. I couldn't read Car and Driver (WebFetch blocked, curl not approved) or the Tom's Guide article body (only navigation came back). The partial overlap is that ChatGPT already knew the 3K front figure. The parking-trigger limit is new.
decides: This tests the brand-launch row rather than overturning it. The G980H still places on 'side cameras' because its two side cameras swivel to face the side windows and record 1080p25 alongside the front and rear. ChatGPT's own follow-up asks whether the shopper means parked damage (door dings, hit-and-runs while parked). For that case, Vortex Radar's finding says the G980H's side cameras won't start a motion-triggered parking clip; only the front camera will. So the G980H fits the 'sideswipes while driving' segment. For parked side damage the honest pointer is a system with exterior side cameras, such as Thinkware's multiplexer with fender-mounted side cameras, which Thinkware says need constant power for parking mode. I found no named measurement showing that any rival's side cameras do trigger parking motion detection, so the page can't claim a measured winner for parked coverage. Separately, the DashCamTalk spec layout shows the REDTIGER F17 Plus, which ChatGPT listed, and the Vantrue N5S both use cabin cameras, not exterior left and right cameras. Neither belongs in a side-camera top three.
